title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

reports.title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

summary:
Robert Jay Josett, 35, a former Costa Mesa police officer, pleaded guilty to misdemeanor charges including unauthorized computer access, repeated annoying calls, and violating a restraining order. After his mistress ended their relationship in April 2024, he contacted her thousands of times by text, phone, and social media over nine months, sometimes more than 100 times in one day, and called her and her new boyfriend up to 58 times daily. He made 13 unauthorized inquiries in the CLETS database on his mistress, a romantic rival, and his wife, and used the FLOCK license plate reader system to track vehicles.

On June 28, 2024, he was served with an emergency protective order and a notice of intent to terminate, then drove by her home and was arrested. Josett was sentenced to three years informal probation and a 52-week domestic violence program, after already spending nine months on a GPS ankle monitor. His law enforcement certification review by POST is pending.
